title: SDK docs scratchpad - to-dos
content:
Quick scratchpad for SDK/docs work - random notes, TODOs, and things to follow up on.

Context:
- Trying to tighten the JS + Python quickstart so new devs can go from signup -> first request < 10 minutes.
- Focus areas: auth examples, streaming responses, error handling, and sample-app (chat widget).

Top priorities (this sprint):
1) Quickstart polish (JS + Python)
   - Current problems: auth snippet uses outdated header format (api_key -> Authorization: Bearer), causing 401s for users who copy-paste. Need to update both README and code samples.
   - Action: update README code blocks, regenerate snippets in docs site.
   - PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/432 (working branch: docs/quickstart-auth)

2) Streaming example for chat (JS)
   - Users report confusion about when to use streaming vs non-streaming. Add a small chat widget sample app that shows incremental UI updates.
   - Tasks:
     * Minimal React example (use EventSource/Fetch readable stream)
     * Add server-side snippet for express that proxies to Redwood hosted API (show SSE/streaming).
     * Add note about reconnect/backpressure and abort controllers.
   - TODO: draft react component and server proxy by end of week.

3) Error codes table in SDK docs
   - Missing mapping of HTTP codes to SDK errors. Need a table: code -> sdk-exception -> recommended handling.
   - Example: 429 -> RateLimitError -> backoff/retry; 503 -> ServiceUnavailable -> retry with exponential backoff; 401 -> AuthenticationError -> surface link to token management docs.

4) Sample app: "NotesAssistant" (simple web app)
   - Purpose: demo embeddings + retrieval + chat. Lightweight, deployable to Vercel.
   - Components:
     * client: React + TypeScript, simple UI, shows embedding calls for search
     * server: Lambda/Edge or simple Node server to handle API keys securely (proxy calls)
     * tests: smoke tests for basic flows
   - Immediate TODOs: create repo skeleton, wire up dev env, add short README with architecture diagram.

Notes / nitty gritty:
- Local dev: make it explicit that devs should set REDWOOD_API_KEY and REDWOOD_API_BASE (for private deployments). Current docs only show API_KEY. Add example .env.
- SDK versioning: mention minimum supported versions of python/js SDKs (e.g., js >= 0.8.0, py >= 0.7.1). Confirm with release-engineering.
- UX copy: replace "apiKey" everywhere with "Redwood API Key" in docs to reduce ambiguity.

Bugs / small fixes to add to backlog:
- Doc code block language tag missing for one python snippet (makes syntax highlighting wrong).
- Python example uses old client constructor: Client(api_key=...) -> needs update to Client(auth_token=...) per new auth lib. Confirm API surface.
- Sample code uses model name "redwood-1" in a couple places; should reference model catalog variable or example stable model name.

Ideas / open questions (ask Alex / Priya):
- Should quickstart show both hosted and dedicated flows? Might overwhelm. Maybe have toggle or two short sections.
- For streaming, do we provide both SSE and WebSocket examples, or just one? Leaning toward SSE + fetch streams to keep complexity low.
- What level of telemetry/observability do we want to demonstrate in sample apps? (basic latency logging vs full tracing).

Possible content for changelog entry when we ship these docs:
- "Improved SDK quickstart: updated auth examples, added streaming chat sample, and published NotesAssistant sample app."

Short-term checklist (next 10 days):
- [ ] Update auth header across JS/Python examples (Mikaela)
- [ ] Draft React streaming chat component (Mikaela + Alex)
- [ ] Create NotesAssistant repo skeleton (Priya)
- [ ] Add error codes table to SDK docs (Samantha)
- [ ] Sync with release-eng on supported SDK versions (ask in #release-eng)

Copy-paste snippets (for inclusion in quickstart) - need verification:
- curl (non-streaming):
  curl -X POST "${REDWOOD_API_BASE:-https://api.redwood.ai}/v1/generate" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY" \
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
    -d '{"model":"open-chat-small","input":"Say hi"}'

- JS fetch streaming (sketch):
  const res = await fetch(`${REDWOOD_API_BASE}/v1/stream`, {
    method: 'POST',
    headers: { 'Authorization': `Bearer ${process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY}`, 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
    body: JSON.stringify({ model: 'open-chat-small', input: "Hello" })
  });
  const reader = res.body.getReader(); // handle chunks -> update UI

Slack / threads to link:
- #dev-docs: convo about quickstart copy (see thread: ts-quickstart-02)
- #sdk-team: streaming API design notes (ask Alex for final API path)

Other misc notes:
- Keep UX first: minimal friction for getting a token and making a single request.
- Consider video 60s quickstart gif to embed in docs later.

Next sync: quick 30m on Thursday to review auth changes and streaming plan. Invite: Alex, Priya, Samantha, ReleaseEng rep.

End of scratchpad.
